main_issue: Whether and how Agent D may keep cooking strong-smelling fish curry in the shared kitchen, given the smell affects the others' work and laundry

A-B.evidence: Both complain about the smell (T1, T2). Both accept weekend-only cooking with advance warning (T8, T10, T13). They never address each other directly.

A-C.evidence: Both complain about the smell (T1, T3). Both accept the weekend arrangement (T11, T13). They never address each other directly.

A-D.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling food (opening). D offered weekends or a warning (T4). A said the weekend is much better and a warning alone is not enough (T5). D agreed to both (T9, T12) and A said 'sounds good' (T13).

B-C.evidence: Both complained about the smell (T2, T3). Both accepted weekends (T10, T11). They did not speak to each other.

B-D.evidence: B asked for weekends plus a heads-up (T8). D agreed to do both (T9). B said 'that works for me' (T10).

C-D.evidence: D asked whether the plan works for C's laundry (T9). C said weekend is fine (T11). D confirmed the arrangement (T12).
